title: Khalsa Authority and the Nawab's Conditions for Relief

blocks.text: Subeg Singh explained that the Nawab had come for protection not merely to save his body, but to test whether the saintly attributes once associated with holy men were now alive within the Khalsa. Bhai Taru Singh, he said, would abide by the Khalsa’s decision, so the Panth treated the appeal as a matter of collective authority rather than private favour.

The Khalsa therefore framed terms before any relief would be granted. The Nawab must restore the twelve villages linked with Amritsar, return the old endowments that had been disturbed, and publicly rename the disputed settlement as Singhpura.

In this way the Panth turned a dying ruler’s plea into a moment of political and spiritual vindication. Mercy would be considered, but only after the Nawab acknowledged the Khalsa’s standing and repaired at least part of the injustice done to Sikh institutions.
